Armitage Auctions, Invermay. Closing Wed 30 Sep 2026

Sleeper tracker

All three auctions are scanned with every photo viewed, and each has a market pass showing sold prices, unsold results and asking prices separately. Only sold prices set a maximum bid. The most solid evidence: 1964 Macallan (lot 768), Ebatarinja watercolour (lot 62), Perth Mint Federation gold and silver coin (lot 876), Cardhu 2020 (lot 677), Tiffany bangle (lot 849) and, if the signature proves genuine, the Haughton Forrest oil (lot 1016). Many lots are already bid at or past their ceilings, and the cards say so. Wine has almost no sold data. Catalogues 4 and 5 exist but have not been scanned. Bids move fast near the close, so check them before you act. Your browser comps are added under "Added from your browser comps" on each lot: most came back as asking prices or category guides, so few maximum bids changed. Two things to note: the gold coin (lot 876) has a melt value of about A$1,700 for its gold centre alone against a $700 bid, and the cautious KEEP ceiling for the Macallan (lot 768) is nearer $3,175 after the lower Whisky Hunter results.

Assumptions
  • Estimates were ignored when scoring, as you asked. Working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD AUD 302 / 1.22 = 247.5, rounded down to 245 (all-in about AUD 299). That comp was in near-fine condition. Working and confidence

Why Medium: The signature is clearly read and there are five close sold results, which would normally give High. It stays at Medium because the prices come from page data rather than a visible 'sold for' line, and the paper condition cannot be judged from the photos.

Dropped entries: None dropped. All seven researcher entries were moved from ASKING to SOLD after the opened pages showed isLotSold true with a final price.

Working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = AUD 150 (For-Auction, Oct 2025). 150 / 1.22 = 122.95, rounded down to $120. All-in at $120 hammer = $146.40. Flip: likely resale = median of close SOLD = $240. Resold through an Australian auction house, assuming 15% seller commission ($36) plus about $10 in lot and photo fees, pickup so $0 outbound postage: net about $194. 194 / 2.44 = 79.5, rounded down to $75. All-in at $75 = $91.50. Caveat: the sold prices come from each Invaluable page's embedded data (isLotSold true, currentBid) because the visible sold line needs a login. I take currentBid on a sold lot to be the hammer.

Ask Armitage: Is there any foxing, fading or staining to the paper? Is the glass intact? Are there any gallery or provenance labels on the back?

Untitled 2024 (Leonard Joel), Approaching Storm January 2026 and the two Stanley 2020 listings moved from ASKING to UNSOLD. Approaching Storm February 2026 moved to SOLD at 425. Country Scene 2025 (190) added. The AASD summary (88 of 124 sold, record 23,318) was snippet only and is not used. The page source shows a 19,000 result for Cliffs in the Megalong Valley in 2022, which is not comparable.

Working: Keep: the lowest close SOLD is AUD 260 (Storm over Nobbys, same 29 x 39 cm board). 260 / 1.22 = 213.1, rounded down to 210. All-in at 210 = 256.20. Flip: likely resale from the close sold evidence is about AUD 300 (Nobbys 260, Bracknell 280, Approaching Storm 425, with yesterday's 110 as a downside warning). Less 20% selling fees (commission plus lot fees) = 240, less 20 for outbound postage and handling = 220. 220 / 2.44 = 90.2, rounded down to 90. All-in at 90 = 109.80. Rate AUD 1.00.
